timeline.jb: Scouts are grading the tape now, and interior linemen get graded on every snap, not the stat line. The agent's work this fall is quiet: film notes, area-scout conversations, nothing that gets in the way of Saturdays.
Your decision. Who represents you, and where you train. Both are your call, and both get made in December.
Senior Bowl and Shrine Bowl invites come through the school and the agent. One week of practices and team meetings, all of it scouted.
Six to eight weeks at a training facility: the 40, the drills, the interviews. The agent sets it up and pays attention; the player does the work.
A few hundred invites. Medicals, interviews, testing. Players who aren't invited run the same numbers at Pro Day.
Your school's day for scouts. You decide what to run again and what to stand on.
Seven rounds. Drafted or signed after, the rookie contract gets negotiated that week.
Relocation, a first budget, insurance, taxes in a new state. The things an agent handles so the player can play.
The one that's actually negotiated. It's where the first four years get paid for.

parentQA.a: Jack, then Ryan. Both have Zach's number. No account manager, no call center. We stay mid-size so he's never in a bigger client's shadow.
The NFLPA caps agent fees at 3% of the playing contract, and ours go in writing before anything is signed. Nothing is paid up front, and fees are only owed on money he actually receives.

parentQA.q: How do you protect what he earns?
parentQA.a: Ryan negotiates the guarantees and injury language. We screen every advisor before he meets them, coordinate taxes, set up disability insurance and build a year-one budget. A good first contract is only the start.

parentQA.q: What happens if he gets hurt?
parentQA.a: Injury settlements, grievances and second opinions are ours to handle. Disability coverage is in place before the first snap.

parentQA.q: What if he's not drafted where we hope?
parentQA.a: It happens, and it isn't the end. Kristian Welch signed with us as an undrafted free agent in 2020 and has played six NFL seasons. The slot decides the first contract; preparation decides the second.

In business since 1986, with six clients who became the highest paid at their position. Jack Tabb played in the NFL, and Ryan Hays is a licensed attorney. We're happy to connect you with current client families.

handle: Rookie deal, extensions, guarantees, fine appeals, grievances. Ryan negotiates the language and guarantees.
Budget in year one. Every advisor and money manager screened before you meet them.
Multi-state filings coordinated. You sign; you don't chase.
Disability policy in place before the first snap. Second medical opinions on us to arrange.
Relocation, housing, car, travel. You land in a city with a place to live.
Interview prep, press, social. Nothing you say gets you in trouble.
Off-season plans, trainer access, recovery. Every year, not just the draft.
Post-career benefits filed, planning done. The career ends; the security doesn't.
